data: Aesthetics is an integral philosophical enquiry which is deeply concerned with our experience of the world and our perception of it. This course will introduce the students to basic concepts in aesthetics and with a focus on the various kinds of aesthetic practices and their entanglement with socio-political, geographical, historical contexts as well as the larger philosophical debates around aesthetics. Concepts of sense perception, beauty, taste, judgment and poetics will be discussed based on core readings including Aristotle, Abhinavagupta, Kant, Bourdieu, Kumaraswamy, and others. A foundational understanding of aesthetics gives students a philosophical grounding in approaching any form of literature and art with the relevant vocabulary and conceptual frame of reference. This will enable students to pursue their interests in engaging with the arts in any way forward - through theory or practice.
